nodes.label: Federation versus Freedom
nodes.source: Collected Works of Babasaheb Ambedkar, Vol. 1
nodes.summary: Kale Memorial Lecture (1939) analyzing the federal scheme of the Government of India Act, 1935, arguing it is not a genuine federation, gives the Indian Princely States disproportionate power over British India, blocks India's path to Dominion Status, and should be rejected in favour of a Federation of British India alone.

nodes.summary: 1953 Times of India article on the creation of linguistic States (prompted by the Andhra agitation), setting out three conditions for forming a linguistic State: viability, awareness of the internal caste/communal composition of the proposed State, and caution against consolidating all speakers of one language into a single unit.

nodes.label: States and Minorities
nodes.source: Collected Works of Babasaheb Ambedkar, Vol. 1
nodes.summary: 1947 memorandum submitted to the Constituent Assembly on behalf of the All India Scheduled Castes Federation, drafted as proposed constitutional articles covering admission of Indian States into the Union, Fundamental Rights of citizens, protections for minorities generally, and specific safeguards (representation, education, settlement) for the Scheduled Castes, including a critique of the Poona Pact's joint-electorate mechanism.

nodes.label: Thoughts on Linguistic States
nodes.source: Collected Works of Babasaheb Ambedkar, Vol. 1
nodes.summary: 1955 response to the States Reorganisation Commission report, arguing its recommendations consolidate the Hindi-speaking North while balkanizing the South, proposing division of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra into smaller units, a separate Bombay City State, cumulative voting to protect minorities within linguistic States, and a second (southern) national capital at Hyderabad.
